requirements.description: Quarterly EPS Surprise History rows aligned by official ticker and announcement date to construct the author’s standardized unexpected-earnings score.

routes.description: The catalog tables are product candidates, not verified matches to the author Surprise History schema. The code keeps EPS/QTR rows, uses OFTIC/ANNDATS/PYEAR/PMON and ACTUAL/SURPMEAN/SURPSTDEV/SUESCORE, and derives surprise ranks; the 2022-04-15 suffix is extract provenance.
routes.expected_period: Quarterly EPS forecast periods. The code aligns to the nearest forecast period on/after ANNDATS, then ranks the surprise measure by YEAR_QUARTER across the supplied file. Its first/last forecast year remains unspecified; 2022-04-15 is extract provenance.

issues.description: The assigned inventory has ten data-identifier CSVs, two documents, and 28 code containers, but no author-prepared full analysis datasets or raw source snapshots. The product-specific routes are therefore unverified.

The datasheet records an ISSDD purchase in February 2022, while the master’s filename macro is 2021-10-01. These dates describe purchase timing and a source-file key, not contradictory release dates. The macro-to-release mapping, exact monthly fields, and coverage remain unverified.

The current master merges against a prepared 2021-09-17 archive match file referenced in the source but not produced by the assigned workflow or included in the assigned inventory. Its schema and compatibility remain unknown.

The main Stata and table files use YOUR_PATH/YOUR_DIRECTORY macros and reset Stata ado directories; Python stages use [redacted-path-17bc19b2c3b1] and [redacted-path-b4e6409b103a] files also use different directory roots (including the press-release text file, matching CSV, all-call exposure CSV, and return datasets).

The SAS bridge creates a work.es4 event-window dataset with event and return fields, then exports it to a Windows es4.dta path; Stata expects a differently named file under its configured intermediate tree. Align the same supported producer/consumer dataset by staging path/name and confirm period/fields before running.

The SAS source contains an opaque connection/setup block withheld by the secret-safe scan. Its connection behavior and required table availability were not assessed, and the existing SAS environment record is unverified.

Drivers import diversity_regex while the supplied regex helper is named 0_racial_diversity_regex.py. The notebook imports commons.components and commons.utils, while the provided component inherits DenseLayer without a local import/definition. These names may be supplied by an external author namespace, so availability is not inferred; exact module/source/version/export contracts are unresolved.

The press parser refers to DIR when resolving its already named relative dictionaries/LM paths. Bind DIR to the project root during ordinary path setup; the dictionary files and their content/version remain a separate input requirement.

The stage writes blank labels and the random 1,000-row workbook is selected with sentence and initiatives fields, while the notebook later expects both initiatives and past_actions. The author-edited label file, annotation instructions, and final schema are not supplied.

The notebook’s training output must be staged where its later cell looks for checkpoints: lightning_logs/initiatives/checkpoints. This is a known path/root setup; the callback uses val_loss with mode=min. File-selection semantics when multiple checkpoints exist are tracked separately.

The two standalone Python table scripts call tqdm but their complete import sections do not import tqdm. The distribution is present, but a direct script run has no documented external namespace setup for this name.
The Python code calls NLTK sentence tokenization; the matching punkt/punkt_tab resources are not covered by package metadata and were not inspected.

The notebook configures Lightning Trainer with gpus=1, num_nodes=0, and max_epochs=200. GPU availability and compatibility of these legacy arguments with the installed PyTorch Lightning API are unverified; preserve the authored settings until compatibility is established.

The notebook searches lightning_logs/initiatives/checkpoints and takes one .ckpt entry through os.listdir(...).pop(). The callback monitors val_loss with mode=min, but behavior with multiple/default-versioned checkpoint files and correspondence to the selected minimum is not specified. Preserve the same model definitions and manual labels; do not guess a selector.
